Source: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D212003
Access: readable in browser on2026-10-06T19:10:50.939Z.

Full browser Event Timeline inspected, including expanded older changes and inline requests. Accepted after changes. Reviewer requested typed JSDoc for moved getUsageText, += for string accumulation, a real label for the select, an HTML grid rather than XUL boxes inside HTML, and one container for show/hide. Use established subkeys terminology instead of inventing composite/secondary terminology. Author rebutted hiding by default because later showing could leave OK/Cancel outside initial window size; final shows then hides for simple mode. A proposed per-element hide loop was removed after fixing the container. Reviewer reproduced failed subkey expiry with automatic-passphrase mode disabled; primary key had to be unlocked as signature authority. Separate unlock/edit fingerprint sets fixed it. Cached automatic unlocking while key-details dialog was open had masked the missing unlock. Reviewer also requested keeping invalid-key errors visible rather than silently closing. Final review accepted after manual combinations; no new automated test in this commit.

Exact source excerpts:
> We should use the occasion to add JSDocs here so that inline comment can turn into proper function documentation.

> suggestion: would all of these string addition benefit from using +=?

> The paragraph should be the label for the select otherwise this is not accessible.

> We're in a pure HTML context so XUL boxes are not styled correctly.

> Having a single element container allows you to hide/show it more easily without needing to loop through all the element IDs.

> I don't think you should close for these error conditions.

> We always must unlock the primary key, because that's the one used for creating a new signature containing the expiration information.

> It now uses separate lists of fingerprints that need to be unlocked (gFingerprintsToUnlock) and edited (gFingerprintsToEdit).

> If that mode is enabled, at the time we open the key details dialog, we test whether the key can get automatically unlocked.

> (And it will remain unlocked until the dialog is closed.)

> If the above feature is disabled, we don't attempt to unlock early.
